_meta.name: English
_meta.about: doodledoggo.app, the introduction site of Doodle Doggo. English is the source. To translate: copy this file to site/i18n/<lang>.json (ja, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ko, es, pt-BR, fr, de, th, id), set _meta.lang and _meta.name, translate the values (never the keys), delete _notes if you like, and set _meta.complete to true when every key is done. A missing key shows the English text. Check with: node tools/site_i18n.js --report
_meta.syntax: Messages use the ICU MessageFormat subset: {name} is a placeholder (keep it exactly, move it where your grammar needs it), {n, plural, one {...} other {...}} and {x, select, a {...} other {...}}. Inside a plural, # is the number. Only ... and ... may be used as markup in a value. anything else is shown as text. Apostrophes are plain text (isn't is fine). { and } are always syntax. Korean may use {name, josa, 이/가} for the particle after a name (game/i18n/msg.js).
_meta.japanese: The site has small Japanese touches for visitors who love dogs: Japanese words with their reading, like 犬 inu = dog. They come in through placeholders such as {inu} or {asobo}. Keep the placeholder and translate the meaning around it (= dog). On the Japanese page you may drop the reading and write the word yourself.
_meta.names: Breed names come from game/i18n/glossary/<lang>.json (breeds), not from this file. Dog names (dog.<key>.name) are the dogs' own names: most languages keep them as they are.

_notes.common.play: The big button that opens the game on itch.io. Capitals are the look. Keep it short (about 18 characters or fewer looks best). itch.io is a website name: never translate it.
_notes.common.logo_alt: Alt text of the logo picture. The game's name, Doodle Doggo, is never translated.
_notes.footer.contact: Footer link that opens an email to contact@doodledoggo.app. Short, capitals are the look.
_notes.footer.credit: an9ou is the maker's name and Claude is the AI assistant. Keep both names as they are.
_notes.lang.label: The language menu's button reads the language's own name (English, 日本語 ...). This text is only read aloud by screen readers.
_notes.home.title: The browser tab title and the search result title. About 60 characters at most. Doodle Doggo is the game's name: keep it.
_notes.home.description: The text under the title in search results. About 155 characters at most.
_notes.home.og_title: The title of a link shared on social media. Usually just the game's name.
_notes.home.og_description: The text of a link shared on social media. About 100 characters.
_notes.home.tagline: The big line under the logo (the crayon emoji in front of it is added by the page). 40 characters looks best.
_notes.home.nav.dogs: Three chips under the tagline (home.nav.dogs, home.nav.japan, home.nav.profiles), each about 16 characters at most so they fit on a phone.
_notes.home.toss: Button under the live playroom: throws another ball for the dogs (the tennis ball emoji in front of it is added by the page).
_notes.home.playroom_caption: {asobo} is the Japanese word 遊ぼう with its reading (asobō). Translate let's play.
_notes.home.free_title: Tooltip on the red stamp 無料: its reading and meaning.
_notes.home.free_line: {muryo} is the Japanese word 無料 with its reading (muryō) = free.
_notes.home.dogs.title: Section title, short (about 20 characters).
_notes.home.dogs.gloss: {inu} is the Japanese word 犬 with its reading (inu). Translate dog.
_notes.home.dogs.lead: {count} is the number of dogs (35 in digits, the English page writes it as a word). The dog count must come from the placeholder, never typed in.
_notes.home.dogs.all: Button. {count} is the number of dogs (35). A plural is fine: {count, plural, other {# ...}}.
_notes.home.feat.walks.text: {osanpo} is the Japanese word お散歩 with its reading. Translate a walk.
_notes.home.japan.caption: {fujisan} is 富士山 with its reading Fuji-san. Mt. Fuji Lookout is the name of a place in the game: use the game's name for it (glossary).
_notes.home.note.shiba.text: {shibainu} is 柴犬 (Shiba Inu written in Japanese). inu is the Japanese word for dog: keep it in italics.
_notes.home.note.lead.text: {dogrun} is ドッグラン with its reading doggu ran (a fenced dog run).
_notes.home.note.shrine.text: {torii} is 鳥居 (a torii gate). torii is the Japanese word: keep it in italics.
_notes.home.words.inu: The little Japanese dictionary: each value is the meaning of one Japanese word, shown after the word and its reading (犬 inu: dog). Translate only the meaning.
_notes.home.trip.text: Shibuya and Asakusa are places in Tokyo: use their usual names in your language.
_notes.home.footer.thanks: {arigato} is ありがとう with its reading arigatō. Translate thank you!
_notes.dogs.title: Browser tab title of the dogs page, about 60 characters at most.
_notes.dogs.description: Search result text. {count} is the number of dogs (35).
_notes.dogs.og_description: {count} is the number of dogs (35 in digits, the English page writes it as a word).
_notes.dogs.h1_gloss: {inutachi} is 犬たち with its reading inu-tachi. Translate the dogs.
_notes.dogs.lead: {count} is the number of dogs (35 in digits, the English page writes it as a word). Katakana is the Japanese script for words from other languages.
_notes.card.alt: Alt text of a dog's picture. {name} is the dog's name (Mochi), {breed} the breed name from the glossary (Shiba Inu).
_notes.card.type: Under the dog's name on its card: {breed} is the breed name (Shiba Inu), {jp} the breed in Japanese (柴犬). On the Japanese page you may leave out {jp} if it repeats {breed}.
_notes.card.more: Link to the dog's full profile, short.
_notes.profile.pup_alt: {name} is the dog's name. {article} is a (or an) for English only: other languages ignore it, e.g. {name}'s puppy.
_notes.profile.pup_cap: The small caption under the puppy picture. Same placeholders as profile.pup_alt.
_notes.profile.jpline: {jp} is the breed in Japanese (柴犬), {reading} its reading (shiba inu), {name} the dog's name, {nameJp} the dog's name in katakana (モチ). Never translate the Japanese parts.
_notes.profile.play: {text} is what the dog does in the Shelter Playroom (dog.<key>.play).
_notes.profile.fun: {mame} is 豆知識 with its reading mame-chishiki (a little bit of knowledge).
_notes.soon.line: Japanese Chin and Kai Ken are breed names (see the glossary if they are there). No dates and no promises of when.
_notes.dog.shiba.name: The dog's own name (as in the game). Most languages keep it. Same for every dog.<key>.name. Each dog is a girl or a boy, the same in every language (sex in tools/site_dogs.js): girls are Pepper (mutt), Mikan (pom), Saffron (afghan), Peaches (pitbull), Maple (malamute), Madeleine (stdpoodle), Toffee (yorkie), Meringue (bichon) and Marshmallow (maltese). Every other dog is a boy. Make adjectives and pronouns agree (French elle/douce, German sie/ihr).
_notes.dog.shiba.quote: The dog's own line, in its voice, short and funny. Every dog.<key>.quote: about 60 characters at most.
_notes.dog.shiba.trait1: A short trait (one or two words), shown in bold, with its line (trait1_line) under it. Same for trait1 to trait4 of every dog.
_notes.dog.shiba.love1: The dog's three favourite things (love1 to love3), each a short noun, lowercase in English.
_notes.dog.shiba.fun: A fun fact. Mochi is also a Japanese rice cake. Keep the Japanese in brackets as it is.
_notes.play.bark.shiba: The barks: what a dog says in a speech bubble in the live playroom. Very short (12 characters or fewer). Same for every play.* key.
_notes.play.bark.chihuahua: ワン！ is the Japanese woof. Keep it, or use your language's woof.
_notes.privacy.updated: {date} is the date of the policy, written by the site in your language's format. an9ou is the maker's name.
_notes.reset.text: Forgot your password? is the name of the button in the game: use the game's translation for it.
_notes.notfound.title: The 404 page title when a page does not exist. Woof? is a dog's puzzled bark.
_notes.common.quoted: Quotation marks around a dog's line. {text} is the line. Use your language's quotation marks (「{text}」, „{text}“, « {text} »).
_notes.nav.label: Screen-reader name of the page menu at the top of every page.
_notes.nav.home: The four page links at the top of every page (nav.home, nav.dogs, nav.map, nav.about). Very short: about 10 characters each, so all four fit on a phone.
_notes.nav.menu: The phone's menu button (☰) label, read aloud by screen readers and shown next to the icon on small phones.
_notes.home.widget.title: Screen-reader title of the itch.io box on the home page. itch.io is a website name: never translate it.
_notes.home.widget.fallback: A plain link under the itch.io box, for when the box does not show (some browsers block it).
_notes.map.h1_gloss: {chizu} is the Japanese word 地図 with its reading (chizu) = map. Keep the placeholder as it is.
_notes.map.shot_alt: Alt text of each place's picture. {place} is the place's name (map.place.*.name).
_notes.map.place.yard.name: The place names: use the game's own names for them (glossary terms) so players recognise them. Same for every map.place.*.name.
_notes.map.place.yard.text: One or two short, cozy sentences about the place. Same for every map.place.*.text.
_notes.map.place.shibuya.text: Hachikō is the real loyal Akita whose statue stands at Shibuya Station. Use his usual name in your language.
_notes.map.place.asakusa.name: Sensō-ji is the temple in Asakusa (浅草寺). Use its usual name in your language.
_notes.about.p1: The owner's own story in eight paragraphs (about.p1 to about.p8), the maker, an9ou, writing in the first person to the players. Translate it warmly and naturally, keeping its feeling, as a person would tell it in your language, not word for word. Keep the eight paragraphs. Use your language's quotation marks in p1.
_notes.about.p5: Keep it in the present tense: the game is free, with no in-game purchases and no ads. No promises about the future (no never, forever or always).
_notes.about.p7: itch.io is a website name: never translate it. A donation is optional: never make it sound like paying is needed.
_notes.about.p8: The page adds a paw print after this last line itself (no emoji in the strings).
_notes.common.close: The button that closes a dog profile pop-up.
_notes.home.game_label: Name of the game box on the home page (read by screen readers). Doodle Doggo is never translated.
_notes.home.fullscreen: Button under the game that makes it fill the screen. Short, about 14 characters.
_notes.home.fullscreen_exit: Label of the ✕ button that leaves full screen (read by screen readers).
_notes.home.game_saves: Small line next to the full screen button.
_notes.home.nojs: Shown in the game box only when the browser has JavaScript off, followed by a link to the itch.io page (its text is footer.play_itch). Doodle Doggo and JavaScript are never translated.
_notes.nav.guide: The fifth page link (the How to play guide). Very short, about 10 characters.
_notes.footer.guide: Footer link to the guide page.
_notes.guide.lead: Guide page intro. Keep it warm and simple.

home.title: Doodle Doggo: a cozy crayon dog game
home.description: Adopt a wobbly crayon pup to love. Walks, cuddles, a garden and kitchen, puppy playdates and a sketchbook town under Mt. Fuji. Free to play in your browser.
home.og_description: Adopt a wobbly crayon pup to love. Free to play in your browser.
home.tagline: Adopt a wobbly crayon pup to love
home.playroom_alt: The Shelter Playroom from the game: bunting, a toy shelf, a basket of toys and floor cushions, with crayon dogs playing
home.playroom_caption: Live from the game’s Shelter Playroom · {asobo} = let’s play!
home.free_line: Free ({muryo}). Plays in your browser on a computer or a phone. No ads.
home.intro: Doodle Doggo is a cozy dog game in a pencil sketchbook. Adopt a deliberately crude crayon dog, care for them, walk them around a little town under Mt. Fuji, grow a garden, cook dog-safe treats and invite friends over for puppy playdates. Nothing bad ever happens.
home.game_saves: Your game saves in this browser.
home.nojs: Doodle Doggo needs JavaScript to play.
home.dogs.title: Meet the dogs
home.dogs.lead: {count} wobbly friends, each with a personality of their own. Tap a dog for the full profile.
home.do.title: What you’ll do
home.feat.walks.title: Walks
home.feat.walks.text: Stroll the sketchbook town, sniff everything, find treasure and earn coins. {osanpo} = a walk.
home.feat.cuddles.title: Cuddles
home.feat.cuddles.text: Pet, feed, bathe and nap. Your pup remembers every belly rub.
home.feat.garden.title: Garden & kitchen
home.feat.garden.text: Grow carrots and pumpkins, then cook treats that are safe for dogs.
home.feat.playdates.title: Puppy playdates
home.feat.playdates.text: Real coat genetics, wonderfully ugly puppies, and kind families for each one.
home.feat.winter.title: Winter & New Year
home.feat.winter.text: Snow days, winter lights, an ugly sweater contest and a Japanese New Year.
home.feat.fuji.title: Mt. Fuji
home.feat.fuji.text: A little town under Mt. Fuji, with a hill to climb for the view.
home.japan.title: Dogs in Japan
home.japan.lead: Doodle Doggo has a little Japanese style. Here are a few friendly notes for visitors who love dogs.
home.japan.fuji_alt: The Mt. Fuji Lookout from the game: Mt. Fuji over a lake, a red torii, stone lanterns and a bench
home.japan.caption: The Mt. Fuji Lookout, in the game {fujisan}
home.note.hachiko.title: Hachiko at Shibuya
home.note.hachiko.text: Hachikō was an Akita who met his person, Professor Ueno, at Shibuya Station every day. After the professor died in 1925, Hachikō kept coming back for almost ten years. His bronze statue stands by the station today, and “meet at Hachikō” is a favourite way to meet friends.
home.note.shiba.title: Shiba and Akita
home.note.shiba.text: Both are native Japanese dogs. The Shiba is the smallest of Japan’s native breeds and the Akita the largest. In Japanese, “Shiba Inu” is {shibainu}: inu means dog.
home.note.cafe.title: Dog cafés
home.note.cafe.text: Many cities have dog-friendly cafés where people bring their own dogs, and some cafés have friendly resident dogs to meet. Each café has its own rules, so read the sign and let the dogs come to you.
home.note.stroller.title: Strollers and carts
home.note.stroller.text: In busy cities you will often see small dogs riding in pet strollers. It keeps small paws off hot summer pavements and out of the crowds, gives older dogs a rest, and trains and many shops ask that pets stay in a carrier.
home.note.lead.title: On a lead in the park
home.note.lead.text: Dogs stay on a lead in parks and on the street. Off-lead running happens in fenced dog runs ({dogrun}). Owners tidy up after their dogs, and many carry a little bottle of water to rinse where their dog peed.
home.note.shrine.alt: A red torii and a small shrine from the game
home.note.shrine.title: At shrines and temples
home.note.shrine.text: Some shrines and temples don’t allow dogs, while others welcome them, and a few even hold blessings for pets. Look for a sign at the entrance, often by the torii gate ({torii}), and when in doubt, ask.
home.words.title: A little Japanese for dog lovers
home.trip.title: Coming up: the Tokyo Trip
home.trip.text: A future update takes your crayon dog on a trip to Tokyo: Shibuya, Asakusa and new friends to meet along the way. We will share more when it is ready.
home.peek.title: A peek inside
home.peek.yard_alt: The yard in winter, a crayon dog by its house
home.peek.walk_alt: A walk through town with Mt. Fuji behind
home.peek.newyear_alt: New Year decorations in the yard

privacy.title: Doodle Doggo privacy
privacy.description: Doodle Doggo has no ads and no tracking. What an account keeps, and how to delete it.
privacy.updated: Last updated: {date}. A game by an9ou.
privacy.short: In short: Doodle Doggo has no ads and no tracking. If you make an account, we keep your email, a scrambled version of your password and your game save and, only if you switch on a Dog Card, the card and the paws it gets. Nothing else.
privacy.collect.title: What we collect
privacy.collect.guest: If you play as a guest: your game is saved in your browser, on your device. We never see it. If you are online, a guest copy is also kept with the login service so it isn't lost, with no email or name attached.
privacy.collect.account: If you make an account, we store:
privacy.collect.email: your email address, so you can log in. We only ever email you when you ask for a 6-digit code to reset your password (Forgot your password? in the game).
privacy.collect.hash: a hashed password. A hash is a scrambled version of your password that can't be turned back into the password. We can't read your password, and nobody else can either.
privacy.collect.save: your game save, so you can play the same game on any device.
privacy.collect.dates: the dates of your account and your latest save.
privacy.collect.nothing_else: We don't collect your name, your age, your location, your contacts or anything else.
privacy.dont.title: What we don't do
privacy.dont.tracking: No tracking, no analytics and no cookies. The only thing loaded from anyone else is the game's handwriting fonts, from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com). Like any website your browser fetches something from, Google can see your IP address when the fonts load.
privacy.itch: The home page has a box from itch.io, where the game is played. It only loads if you tap it, and then itch.io's own privacy policy applies.
privacy.dont.share: We never sell, rent or share your data with anyone.
privacy.dont.email: No newsletters. The only email is the 6-digit password reset code you ask for.
privacy.cards.title: Dog Cards
privacy.cards.lead: With an email account you can share a Dog Card, so your dogs visit other players' Dog Park and Yoyogi dog run. It is off until you switch it on in Settings.
privacy.cards.see: What other players see: the two-word card name you pick from a list, your dogs' drawings, breeds, coats and outfits, the card name you pick for each dog (its own name only when that name is on our list), and how many paws the card got.
privacy.cards.never: Never shown: your email, your account, or anything you typed. Cards have no free text at all: every part is picked from a fixed list, so there is nothing to read or reply to.
privacy.cards.paws: Paws: any player can give a card one paw a day. We keep who gave a paw for a few days, only so each player gives one a day.
privacy.cards.off: Turning it off deletes the card and its paws as soon as the game is online. Hide this card in the game stops a card visiting you. Deleting your account deletes your card too.
privacy.where.title: Where it is kept
privacy.where.text: Account data and saves are stored with Cloudflare, who run the login service. Password emails are sent through Resend, who handle only that one email. Both keep the data only to do that job. You play on itch.io, and the game runs in your browser. itch.io has its own privacy policy for its own site.
privacy.children.title: Children
privacy.children.text: Doodle Doggo is a gentle game for everyone. If you are young, please ask a grown-up before making an account. You never need an account: guest play is complete.
privacy.choices.title: Your choices
privacy.choices.guest: Play as a guest at any time, with no account.
privacy.choices.export: Export a save code in Settings whenever you like, to keep your own copy.
privacy.delete: Delete your account and everything we hold: write to {mail} from the email address you signed up with, and say you want your account deleted. We delete the account, the password hash, the saves and any Dog Card, and tell you when it is done. This doesn't remove a save code you exported or the guest save on your own device. You can clear those yourself.
privacy.choices.ask: Ask what we hold about you in the same way.
privacy.changes.title: Changes
privacy.changes.text: If this policy changes in a way that matters, we will put the new date at the top and a short note on the game's page.
privacy.contact.title: Contact
reset.title: Doodle Doggo: forgot your password?
reset.text: Password resets now happen in the game: tap Forgot your password? and use the code we email you.

dog.shiba.name: Mochi
dog.shiba.quote: I could leave anytime. I choose not to.
dog.shiba.play: Keeps a little distance, then wanders over on Mochi’s own terms.
dog.shiba.fun: Mochi is also the Japanese word for a soft rice cake (餅). The Shiba is one of Japan’s own native dogs.
dog.corgi.name: Biscuit
dog.corgi.quote: Is that a snack? Is everything a snack?
dog.corgi.play: Sits by the bowl and looks at you. Then the bowl. Then you.
dog.golden.name: Sunny
dog.golden.quote: I love you. Who are you?
dog.golden.trait2_line: brings the ball, then a stick
dog.golden.play: Always brings the ball back, and races the hardest to get it.
dog.dachs.name: Noodle
dog.dachs.quote: The rest of me is on its way.
dog.dachs.trait1_line: naps like it is a job
dog.dachs.trait2_line: squeaks the duck till you look
dog.dachs.trait4_line: the rest of him is on its way
dog.dachs.play: The neediest in the room: the pet me eyes, full power. Then a little digging.
dog.husky.name: Frost
dog.husky.trait3_line: serenades the moon and the sofa
dog.husky.play: Talks and talks. The topic is usually pets. A-woo-woo.
dog.mutt.name: Pepper
dog.mutt.quote: Hi. Can I come home with you?
dog.mutt.trait2_line: asks with a tiny paw tap
dog.mutt.trait4_line: waits by the door, just in case
dog.mutt.play: Gentle, and always drifts towards you. Just wants to be near.
dog.mutt.fun: A rescue dog in Japanese is 保護犬 (hogoken).
dog.chihuahua.name: Peanut
dog.chihuahua.play: Stands guard by the gate and reports every passer-by.
dog.pug.name: Dumpling
dog.pug.play: Naps a lot. Rolls over now and then: the belly is open for business.
dog.greyhound.name: Rocket
dog.greyhound.personality: Gentle couch potato who sprints in bursts.
dog.greyhound.play: Naps, then a sudden burst of zoomies. The fastest to any ball.
dog.beagle.name: Bagel
dog.beagle.quote: Smelled that from three streets away.
dog.beagle.trait1_line: follows a smell, forgets the rest
dog.beagle.trait3_line: bays at squirrels and at nothing
dog.beagle.play: Sniffs everything. Then sniffs you, and bays a tiny hello.
dog.poodle.name: Pretzel
dog.poodle.personality: Thinks it is the smartest one in the room. It is.
dog.poodle.trait1_line: learns it before you finish teaching
dog.poodle.play: Sits politely and waits. Offers a paw, ever so politely.
dog.collie.name: Scout
dog.collie.quote: Will herd the puppies, the ducks and the furniture.
dog.collie.personality: Has counted the sheep. There are no sheep. Has counted you.
dog.collie.play: Circles the other dogs and nudges them together. You are part of the flock.
dog.samoyed.name: Cloud
dog.samoyed.quote: Sheds a second dog every spring.
dog.samoyed.personality: Smiles so the snow does not stick. Also just smiles.
dog.samoyed.trait4_line: cold water is the best water
dog.samoyed.play: Social and smiley, tags along with the pack. Hard to say no to.
dog.frenchie.name: Brioche
dog.frenchie.quote: Sofa. Cushion. Your foot. All good seats.
dog.frenchie.personality: Snores, snorts, sits on your foot. All three at once.
dog.frenchie.trait1_line: a tiny engine at nap time
dog.frenchie.trait2_line: your foot is now his seat
dog.frenchie.play: Short, cheeky zoomies, and a likely ball thief. Then sits on your foot.
dog.akita.name: Kuma
dog.akita.quote: I will wait for you. I am very good at waiting.
dog.akita.personality: Calm, loyal, quietly proud. Waits by the gate.
dog.akita.trait1_line: waits at the gate for you
dog.akita.play: Sits quietly at the gate or the front, facing you. Never barks, always waiting.
dog.akita.fun: The Akita is a native dog of Japan. Hachikō, the famous dog who waited at Shibuya Station, was an Akita.
dog.spitz.name: Daifuku
dog.spitz.quote: Yes, I am this white on purpose. Look at me.
dog.spitz.personality: A white fluffball, cheerful, a bit of a show-off.
dog.spitz.trait1_line: walks to the front and poses
dog.spitz.trait4_line: a good brush keeps it soft
dog.spitz.play: Trots to the front of the room and strikes a happy pose. Then waits for applause.
dog.spitz.fun: Daifuku is a soft, round rice sweet (大福). The Japanese Spitz is a Japanese dog type, and it is always white.
dog.pom.name: Mikan
dog.pom.quote: Yip! That was my indoor voice.
dog.pom.personality: A tiny fluffy loudspeaker. Spins when happy.
dog.pom.trait1_line: a small dog with big opinions
dog.pom.trait4_line: leads dogs ten times its size
dog.pom.play: Spins in a happy circle, three or four times, with a little yip.
dog.pom.fun: Mikan is the Japanese word for a mandarin orange (みかん), a good name for an orange fluffball.
dog.afghan.name: Saffron
dog.afghan.quote: I do not fetch. I glide.
dog.afghan.personality: Elegant and aloof. Not one hair out of place.
dog.afghan.trait1_line: not one hair out of place
dog.afghan.trait3_line: a brush a few times a week
dog.afghan.play: Keeps to the open, sunny spots and likes a good run. Then drapes elegantly on a cushion.
dog.dane.name: Waffle
dog.dane.quote: I am a lap dog. Your lap is just too small.
dog.dane.personality: A gentle giant who follows you from room to room.
dog.dane.trait3_line: leans on you for a hug
dog.dane.play: Follows you around the room, then flops by the bed or the front. Careful with the tail.
dog.mastiff.name: Crumpet
dog.mastiff.quote: A little drool is how I say I love you.
dog.mastiff.personality: Huge, slow and sweet. Naps in the biggest patch of shade.
dog.mastiff.trait2_line: huge and soft as a cushion
dog.mastiff.trait3_line: a towel for that big face
dog.mastiff.trait4_line: one big sigh at a time
dog.mastiff.play: Naps by the bed or in the shade. Moves only for snacks, and only slowly.
dog.gsd.name: Strudel
dog.gsd.quote: Ears up. On duty. Was that a squirrel?
dog.gsd.personality: Clever and alert. Loves a job, any job.
dog.gsd.trait1_line: learns a trick in a minute
dog.gsd.play: Rounds up the pack and guards the gate. Loves a job, any job.
dog.dobie.name: Espresso
dog.dobie.quote: I am on guard. Please guard me with a blanket.
dog.dobie.personality: A big softie in a sleek coat. Keeps watch, then wants a cuddle.
dog.dobie.play: Patrols the gate and the front, then comes in for a cuddle.
dog.dobie.fun: Espresso is the small, strong coffee (エスプレッソ). The Doberman here keeps its natural floppy ears and long tail, just as nature drew them.
dog.corso.name: Cannoli
dog.corso.quote: I am very serious. Except when you scratch my ears.
dog.corso.personality: A calm, gentle guardian. Keeps an eye on the whole family.
dog.corso.trait1_line: a friendly hill with a heartbeat
dog.corso.trait2_line: keeps an eye on the whole family
dog.corso.trait4_line: jowls have a mind of their own
dog.corso.play: Stands by the gate or rests in the shade, calm and steady, keeping watch.
dog.corso.fun: Cannoli is the crispy Sicilian pastry. The Cane Corso is an old Italian guardian dog, and a very gentle one.
dog.pitbull.name: Peaches
dog.pitbull.quote: My whole back half wags. I cannot stop it.
dog.pitbull.personality: A wiggly, people-loving goofball. Every stranger is a new best friend.
dog.pitbull.trait2_line: leans in for a long one
dog.pitbull.trait3_line: every stranger is a best friend
dog.pitbull.play: Wiggles over for a hug, then asks for another. Plays hard, cuddles harder.
dog.minpin.name: Jellybean
dog.minpin.quote: I am not small. Everything else is big.
dog.minpin.personality: A tiny, fearless bundle of energy. Prances everywhere.
dog.minpin.trait3_line: tells big dogs what to do
dog.minpin.play: Zooms in short bursts, then prances over like a very small horse.
dog.lab.name: Butter
dog.lab.quote: Is it dinner? It feels like dinner.
dog.lab.personality: Friendly, food-loving and always ready for a swim.
dog.lab.play: Hangs around the food bowl and the open lawn, hoping for a snack or a ball.
dog.lab.fun: Butter is bata (バター) in Japanese. The Labrador is one of the most popular dogs in the world, and the favourite helper dog in Japan.
dog.malamute.name: Maple
dog.malamute.personality: A big fluffy sled dog who talks back. Loves snow and digging.
dog.malamute.trait4_line: shade and water on warm days
dog.malamute.play: Chats from the shade, then goes off to dig a hole. A long, friendly woo-woo.
dog.chow.name: Bao
dog.chow.quote: I am not grumpy. This is just my face.
dog.chow.personality: A dignified fluffy lion with a blue tongue. Picks friends carefully.
dog.chow.play: Keeps to the edge and the shade. Allows one pat, maybe two.
dog.chow.fun: Bao is a soft steamed bun (包). The Chow Chow comes from China, and its blue-black tongue is completely real.
dog.stdpoodle.name: Madeleine
dog.stdpoodle.quote: I am the big poodle. The small one is my cousin.
dog.stdpoodle.personality: A tall, clever, curly athlete. Learns tricks before you teach them.
dog.stdpoodle.trait1_line: learns a trick before you teach it
dog.stdpoodle.play: Bows politely, runs one elegant lap, then offers a long curly paw.
dog.stdpoodle.fun: Madeleine is the small shell-shaped French cake (マドレーヌ). The Standard Poodle is the big cousin of the Miniature Poodle, Pretzel.
dog.schnauzer.name: Muesli
dog.schnauzer.quote: The beard is for wisdom. And soup.
dog.schnauzer.personality: Bearded, bossy and very alert. Reports every leaf.
dog.schnauzer.play: Stands at the gate or the edge and reports on everything. Wiggles the eyebrows.
dog.westie.name: Shortbread
dog.westie.quote: I was white this morning. I promise.
dog.westie.personality: A cheerful little white terrier. Digs first, asks later.
dog.westie.trait1_line: a carrot tail that never stops
dog.westie.trait4_line: a muddy nose is a badge
dog.westie.play: Sniffs along the edges and digs a polite hole. Trots over with a muddy nose.
dog.yorkie.name: Toffee
dog.yorkie.quote: I am in charge here. Please lift me onto the sofa.
dog.yorkie.personality: A tiny terrier with silky hair and a giant attitude.
dog.yorkie.trait4_line: asks to be lifted onto the sofa
dog.yorkie.play: Demands a pet in a tiny, loud voice, then sits on your foot like a little queen.
dog.bichon.name: Meringue
dog.bichon.quote: Is this a haircut or a cloud? Yes.
dog.bichon.personality: A happy cotton ball who bounces everywhere.
dog.bichon.trait2_line: a cotton ball with a heartbeat
dog.bichon.play: Bounces in, spins once, and waits for applause. Pets count.
dog.bichon.fun: Meringue is the light, airy sweet (メレンゲ). The Bichon Frise is called a “curly lapdog” in French.
dog.maltese.name: Marshmallow
dog.maltese.quote: I do not walk. I float, elegantly.
dog.maltese.personality: A gentle little lap dog in a long white coat.
dog.maltese.trait4_line: keeps the hair out of its eyes
dog.maltese.play: Floats over and sits by you, then looks up through the long white fringe.
dog.maltese.fun: Marshmallow is mashumaro (マシュマロ) in Japanese. The Maltese is a very old lapdog, and very popular in Japan.
dog.shihtzu.name: Wonton
dog.shihtzu.personality: A relaxed lap dog with a top-knot and big opinions about naps.
dog.shihtzu.play: Rolls over in a sunny spot or on a bed. Would like a lap, thank you.
dog.shihtzu.fun: Wonton is the soft dumpling (ワンタン). The Shih Tzu was a palace dog in China, and its name means lion.

about.title: About us · Doodle Doggo
about.description: Why Doodle Doggo was made: a crayon dog for someone who loves dachshunds, which grew into a whole world. Free, with no in-game purchases and no ads.
about.og_description: A crayon dog drawn for someone who loves dachshunds grew into a whole little world. Free, no ads, no in-game purchases.
about.p1: My girlfriend loves dachshunds more than anything in the world. Every time one walks past us on the street, she stops, smiles, and for a moment nothing else matters. I have lost count of how many times she has said, “One day, we'll have one of our own.”
about.p2: But one day isn't today. We don't live on our own yet, and a dog deserves a real home, with space, time and someone there every day. So we wait.
about.p3: I didn't want her to only wait. So I picked up a crayon and drew her a dog. It was wobbly and a little crooked, and she loved it anyway. Then it needed a yard to run in, a bowl to eat from, a town to walk through and friends to play with. Little by little, that one crayon dog grew into this whole world.
about.p4: Doodle Doggo is for her. It is also for everyone who loves dogs but can't have one right now, maybe because of a small apartment, a busy life, a landlord who says no, or simply because the time isn't right yet. Here you can adopt, feed, cuddle and walk your dogs, and nothing bad ever happens to them. Every dog you meet is waiting for someone, just like we are.
about.p5: The game is completely free, with no in-game purchases and no ads. It's a small project made with a lot of love, and it keeps growing. New dogs, places and little surprises arrive with every update.
about.p6: I would truly love to hear from you. Tell me what made you smile, what felt wrong, or what you wish your dog could do. Every comment helps me make the game better.
about.p7: If Doodle Doggo brightens your day and you'd like to support us, you can leave a donation on itch.io. Every bit helps us keep building, and maybe one day it brings us a little closer to a real dachshund of our own.
about.p8: Thank you for playing, and for giving these crayon dogs a home.
about.itch: Leave a comment or a donation on itch.io
guide.title: How to play Doodle Doggo: a guide for new dog owners
guide.description: A short guide to Doodle Doggo: adopt your first dog, keep them happy, earn coins on walks, unlock the garden, the kitchen and Tokyo, and raise puppies.
guide.og_description: Adopt, care, walk, explore: everything a new dog owner needs to know.
guide.lead: Doodle Doggo is a slow, cozy game. There is no way to lose and nothing bad ever happens. Here is everything you need for your first days.
guide.steps.title: Your first day
guide.step1.p: Start at the Shelter. Read each dog’s card, pick a boy or a girl and give them a name. Adopting is always free.
guide.step2.p: Four crayon meters show Hunger, Happiness, Energy and Clean. Feed, Play, Care and Nap fill them, and petting your dog always helps.
guide.step3.p: Walks are where you earn most of your Paw Coins. Dash along the route, jump, collect treats and follow the Nose-o-meter to dig up treasure.
guide.step4.p: Everything you do together adds Bond. Each new Bond level opens a new part of the game.
guide.step5.p: Open the Map to visit the park, the beach, Market Street’s shops, the café and more. Every place has its own lines for every dog.
guide.unlock.title: What Bond opens
guide.unlock.b2: Bond 2: the Garden and the Mt. Fuji Lookout.
guide.unlock.b3: Bond 3: the Kitchen and the Station, where the Shinkansen goes to Tokyo.
guide.unlock.more: Higher Bond: more places your dog likes to hang out around home and town.
guide.tips.title: Handy tips
guide.tip1: Gerald the duck knows everything. Follow his tour on your first day, or read his notes in the Journal later.
guide.tip2: The clipboard in the yard has three daily missions. They are a quick way to earn coins and Bond.
guide.tip3: Ball play works everywhere: drag the ball and let go to throw. Your whole pack races for it.
guide.tip4: Time runs fast: one game hour is one real minute, and one real day is a month in your dog’s life.
guide.tip5: The camera button makes a postcard of your pack to save or share.
guide.tip6: Seasons follow the real calendar, with festivals in autumn, winter and the New Year.
guide.pups.title: Puppies and families
guide.pups.p1: Grown-up dogs can have puppy playdates. Coats and looks are inherited like real dogs, and mixes get a body from one parent and a head from the other.
guide.pups.p2: The game keeps the real welfare rules: no relatives, the right age, rest between litters. Puppies you don’t keep go to named families for free, and they send you postcards.
guide.faq.title: Questions
guide.faq.a1: Yes. It is free to play in your browser, with no ads.
guide.faq.a2: In your browser. Make a free account in Settings to play the same dogs on another device.
guide.faq.q3: Can I play on my phone?
guide.faq.a3: Yes. The game has a phone layout. Use the Full screen button on the home page for the biggest view.
guide.faq.q4: Can my dog get sick or run away?
guide.faq.a4: Never. Meters only go low, your dog just gets a bit sleepy or hungry, and one cuddle starts to fix it.
guide.cta: Ready? The game is waiting on the home page.
